classification.difficultyReason: Find the new input whose transformed argument equals the original coordinate four, accounting for both the translation sign and the negative input multiplier.

content.prompt: Let $P(4,y)$ lie on $y=f(x)$. Find the new $x$-coordinate of $P$ on each of the following.

answer.worked:
Write $y=f\left(2\left(x-\frac12\right)\right)$. Replace $x\mapsto2x$, then $x\mapsto x-\frac12$: dilate horizontally by a factor of $\frac12$, then translate right by $\frac12$ unit.

The new coordinate is
$$\begin{align*}x'&=\frac12(4)+\frac12\\x'&=\frac52.\end{align*}$$

Write $y=f\left(2\left(x+\frac12\right)\right)$. Replace $x\mapsto2x$, then $x\mapsto x+\frac12$: dilate horizontally by a factor of $\frac12$, then translate left by $\frac12$ unit.

The new coordinate is
$$\begin{align*}x'&=\frac12(4)-\frac12\\x'&=\frac32.\end{align*}$$

Write $y=f\left(-2\left(x-\frac12\right)\right)$. Replace $x\mapsto2x$, then $x\mapsto-x$, then $x\mapsto x-\frac12$: dilate horizontally by a factor of $\frac12$, reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate right by $\frac12$ unit.

The new coordinate is
$$\begin{align*}x'&=-\frac12(4)+\frac12\\x'&=-2+\frac12\\x'&=-\frac32.\end{align*}$$

Write $y=f\left(-2\left(x+\frac12\right)\right)$. Replace $x\mapsto2x$, then $x\mapsto-x$, then $x\mapsto x+\frac12$: dilate horizontally by a factor of $\frac12$, reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate left by $\frac12$ unit.

The new coordinate is
$$\begin{align*}x'&=-\frac12(4)-\frac12\\x'&=-2-\frac12\\x'&=-\frac52.\end{align*}$$
